best.plan_strategy: Attempt 2 stays in hist_gbdt but attacks both open axes at once with a much smaller-capacity, heavily regularised fit and a stronger positive weight. Concretely: max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=8, max_depth=3, min_samples_leaf=60, l2_regularization=10.0, early_stopping=false so all 5,026 training rows are fitted, and class_weight={"0":1,"1":9} to push the default cut further toward recall than 'balanced' (ratio 5.07) pinned it. Preprocessing is held bit-for-bit identical to attempt 1 (impute='none' so the estimator splits on NaN natively for expected_num_interested_in_me at 78.5% missing, expected_num_matches at 14% and shared_interests_* at 12.8%; scale=false; no missingness columns), so the whole score delta is attributable to capacity + class weight. Read-outs that direct attempts 3-5: train_val_gap (was 0.2949 — must fall well below 0.15 for the regularisation to have worked), balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut versus 0.7984 (whether shrinking capacity raised or cost ranking), and cut_headroom versus 0.0935 (whether weight 9 landed the cut near-optimally, or overshot into low specificity). If the ranking ceiling stalls near 0.80 while headroom shrinks, attempt 3 swaps to xgboost with subsample/colsample-style regularisation and scale_pos_weight tuned around 8-12; if the ranking rises with capacity cuts, attempt 3 pushes regularisation further in this family.

critic.evidence: hist_gbdt scored balanced_accuracy=0.7049 (95% CI 0.6765~0.7358) against the bar 0.8342 — a shortfall of 0.1293. Training is essentially memorised: train_balanced_accuracy=0.9998, train_f1=0.9988, train_accuracy=0.9996, giving train_val_gap=0.2949 with 400 unregularised-ish iterations (lr=0.06, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=20, l2=1.0, early_stopping=false) on only 5,026 rows with 241 columns. The family swap did raise the ranking: roc_auc 0.8691 vs baseline 0.8505, pr_auc 0.5878 vs 0.5507, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7984 vs baseline ceiling 0.7712 (+0.0272 of ranking ceiling) — so this is not a plateaued family (only 1 attempt in 1 family). Two axes are both still open: cut_headroom=0.0935 of the 0.1293 remaining (72% purchasable at the operating point), and recall=0.4855 sits well below specificity=0.9243, so the positive class needs *more* weight than class_weight='balanced' (ratio ~5.07) pins it at. No hyperparams were dropped (dropped_hyperparams=[]), and runtime is a non-issue (train_time_sec=10.9 of a 600s budget). The immediate limiter is the 0.2949 gap: a model at train 0.9998 is spending capacity on noise, which caps the ranking that the cut then has to work from.
critic.direction: Stay in hist_gbdt and cut the capacity hard while pushing the operating point further toward recall in the same shot — the gap 0.2949 says 400x31-leaf trees are memorising, and recall 0.4855 vs specificity 0.9243 says 'balanced' undershot the cut — so refit with shallower, more regularised trees and an explicit positive weight above 5.07, keeping preprocessing (impute='none', no scaling, no missingness columns) bit-for-bit unchanged so the score stays attributable to capacity+weight.

critic.evidence: Attempt 2 scored balanced_accuracy=0.7990 (95% CI 0.7735~0.8229) against the bar 0.8342 — shortfall 0.0352, and the bar sits outside the CI. The prescribed regularisation worked exactly as intended: train_val_gap fell 0.2949→0.0547 (train 0.8536 vs val 0.7990), and the paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0941 (95% CI +0.0628~+0.1264, P=1.000), so that movement is real and resolved. But almost all of it came off the operating-point axis, not the ranking: balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut moved only 0.7984→0.8050 (+0.0066) while cut_headroom collapsed 0.0935→0.0060. class_weight {0:1,1:9} landed the cut essentially at its optimum — recall 0.8551 vs specificity 0.7429 now has recall *above* specificity, i.e. the weight has slightly overshot, so pushing it further is the wrong direction and pulling it back can only buy ≤0.0060. With 0.0352 still to go, the ledger prices the operating-point lever at 17% of the remaining distance; 83% is ranking, and the ranking ceiling of this configuration is 0.8050, below the bar. Two hist_gbdt points now span ranking ceilings 0.7984→0.8050 (roc_auc 0.8691→0.8736), i.e. ~0.007 of ceiling per retune, so more tuning inside this family cannot cover 0.0292 of ceiling. No hyperparams were dropped (dropped_hyperparams=[]) and runtime is trivial (5.4s train, 8.0s wall of 600s), so nothing is resource-limited. Calibration degraded (brier 0.1063→0.1637, calibration_error 0.0619→0.2193) as expected from the heavy positive weight, but calibration is not the goal and there is no recalibration lever.
critic.direction: Spend attempt 3 on the ranking axis, since the cut is already near-optimal (cut_headroom 0.0060 of the 0.0352 needed): swap to xgboost — the one untried family on the candidate list that also splits NaN natively, so preprocessing stays bit-for-bit identical (impute='none', no scaling, no missingness columns) and the delta is attributable to the family alone — fitted with row/column subsampling and moderate depth to raise roc_auc/balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut above 0.8050, with scale_pos_weight held near the level that already centred the cut (≈7, one notch back from 9 since recall 0.8551 now exceeds specificity 0.7429).

critic.evidence: Attempt 3 (xgboost) scored balanced_accuracy=0.7718 (95% CI 0.7423~0.8007) against the bar 0.8342 — shortfall 0.0624. The paired Δ vs iteration 2 is -0.0272 (95% CI -0.0494~-0.0046, P(better)=0.003), so the family swap measurably *lost* score; the previous wrong_model_family prescription paid nothing. Critically, the ranking did not move at all: balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8050 (hist_gbdt) → 0.8037 (xgboost), a span of only 0.0013 across two families, while the ceiling still needed to rise 0.0292 to reach the bar — the shortfall is 22× the span the two families have covered, and roc_auc barely budged (0.8736 → 0.8759, inside the ~0.003-0.006 paired resolution). In KS terms the bar demands 0.6684 and the best ranking so far is 0.6100. So a third family off the same list is not a plan that reaches the bar. What *did* move is capacity/operating point: train_val_gap rose 0.0547 → 0.1810 (train_balanced_accuracy 0.9527 vs val 0.7718) and cut_headroom reopened 0.0060 → 0.0319, with recall 0.6957 now *below* specificity 0.8479 — scale_pos_weight=7.0 pulled the cut back too far, past the crossing that class_weight 1:9 (recall 0.8551 > specificity 0.7429) sat on. The operating-point lever is worth at most 0.0319 of the 0.0624 remaining (51%); the other 49% is ranking that neither family produced and that the executor cannot add features to. With 5,026 training rows, 241 encoded columns that duplicate each rating with its binned one-hot, expected_num_interested_in_me 78.5% missing, and a ~9:1 class ratio, the bar sits above what any single estimator on these columns has shown it can rank — it exceeds the baseline ranking ceiling 0.7712 by construction and both tried ceilings land ~0.804.
critic.direction: Stop spending iterations on family swaps — two families' ranking ceilings span only 0.0013 against a 0.0292 ceiling shortfall — and instead go back to the best-scoring configuration (iteration 2's hist_gbdt) and reclaim the 0.0319 of reopened cut_headroom by putting the operating point back between the two measured brackets, since recall 0.6957 < specificity 0.8479 at weight 7 while recall 0.8551 > specificity 0.7429 at weight 9 means the optimum is bracketed around ratio ~8 with slightly more capacity than depth 3 allowed.
